4 MapSketch include sketch showing the t: North-oriented map encompassing a 1.5-mile radius centered on CSX Rail Milepost 142.5 and Highway 411. County Line Road is completely closed to public traffic to secure the Staging Area at the County Fairgrounds. The primary incident site is at Rail Milepost 142.5, where freight cars #12 through #18 have jackknifed. Car #14 is a breached tank car releasing a Class 3 flammable and toxic liquid, Benzene, into Whispering Pines Creek at an estimated 20 gallons per minute, with visible surface sheening extending 500 meters downstream. Elevated VOCs are present within a 300-foot downwind plume tracking East-Southeast at 5 mph. Threatened areas include the Whispering Pines Nature Reserve Wetlands one mile downstream and the Municipal Water Intake two miles downstream. Modeled waterborne contamination is moving East at 1.5 knots, requiring immediate defensive booming.
5 Situation Summary and Health and Safet: The derailment occurred at 05:45 due to mechanical rail car failure and caused a secondary 0.5-acre brush fire in the right-of-way that threatens an adjacent intact liquefied petroleum gas tank car. Local law enforcement is executing a mandatory 0.5-mile residential evacuation. Hazards include toxic Benzene inhalation, dermal exposure, flash fires from pooling product, heavy machinery movement around compromised rail lines, responder heat stress in 88°F weather, and slip-and-trip hazards on steep creek banks. A 300-foot Exclusion Zone is established around the rail cars. Hot Zone containment personnel must wear Level B PPE, including SCBA and chemical-resistant clothing. Level C is authorized for Warm Zone booming teams only when continuous photoionization detector monitoring confirms VOCs below 1 ppm. Firefighters must wear full structural turnout gear with SCBA. All personnel must pass through a formal wet decontamination corridor at the Warm-to-Cold Zone interface before leaving the operational area.
7 Current and Planned Objectives: Ensure the life safety of all responders and the public within the perimeter by 09:00; complete the 0.5-mile downwind residential evacuation by 09:30; suppress the brush fire near the liquefied petroleum gas car and eliminate thermal risk by 10:00; deploy effective deflection and underflow containment booming across Whispering Pines Creek to protect the Municipal Water Intake; and formally establish a Unified Command structure by 10:30.
ActionsRow1: County Fire and Sheriff units were initially dispatched, and a 500-foot isolation perimeter was established.
ActionsRow2: Local Fire Chief Thomas established command and notified the State Department of Environmental Quality, the Environmental Protection Agency, and CSX Railroad.
ActionsRow3: The Sheriff's Department initiated door-to-door evacuations of 45 homes.
ActionsRow4: Regional Hazmat Team 1 arrived to deploy an air-monitoring grid and inspect the damaged tanks.
ActionsRow5: Engine 41 and Tanker 5 initiated defensive foam applications on the brush fire.
ActionsRow6: Advance teams from the state environmental agency and the railroad arrived to finalize the water-containment strategy.
ActionsRow7: Deploy a specialized spill contractor to place 500 feet of deflection boom at Boom Site 1.
ActionsRow8: Launch a drone overflight to map downstream tracking.
ActionsRow9: Complete the transition to a fully unified command at the Mobile Command Post.
